relationships.subject: spinal microglia
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, these results indicate a critical role for resident microglia in formalin-induced phase II persistent inflammatory pain as well as bradykinin-induced inflammatory pain.

relationships.subject: spinal microglia
relationships.evidence_quote: We found that microglia ablation significantly decreased c-fos expression in spinal dorsal horn following intraplantar formalin injection

relationships.subject: skin macrophages
relationships.evidence_quote: These results suggest that formalin-induced phase I pain is mainly augmented by skin macrophages important in the immediate inflammatory response.

key_findings: Resident spinal microglia ablation reduced formalin phase II and bradykinin-induced pain and decreased c-fos/pERK in dorsal horn, while peripheral macrophage depletion only reduced phase I.
Spinal microglia increased process motility and outward K+ currents within an hour of formalin.
